clue.text: Ever tossed out a pair of Dockers?

indicators.note: out here means wrong or askew, so the letters of the tossed words are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone throws away a pair of Dockers trousers, apparently for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals rearranging the letters of EVER TOSSED. Dockers is a brand of trousers, but here a pair of dockers is simply two port workers, so the plural answer fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevedores are workers who load and unload ships, which is what dockers do; two of them make a plural.

clue.text: Rod Stewart's outside with a couple of females

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters, here taken from the singer's surname

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: Rod Stewart appears flanked by two women, as rock stars often are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like the singer's first name but is the definition; the 's of Stewart's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a long stick or pole, so a rod is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Getting on Hoskins after retirement? Woof woof!

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for the setter is read backwards

parts.note: the setter of this puzzle, so he refers to himself as me
the sound a dog makes when it is barking

explanation.surface: The setter is getting on in years and wonders if retirement will send him barking mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' suggests ageing, which fits the retirement theme, but it means boarding. Barking is also British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go aboard a ship or plane, so embarking is getting on board.

clue.text: She's the sort to follow you I've been told

indicators.note: something one has been told has been heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the word you, said aloud, gives the sound wanted

explanation.surface: Someone has been told that a certain woman is the type to follow you around.
explanation.walkthrough: A female sheep is a she, and sheep are proverbial followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is famously a follower of the flock, so she is the sort to follow.

clue.text: What Hoskins does to Serpent for starters?

definitions.meaning: Hoskins and Serpent are both Independent setters, so Hoskins claims to out-set his colleague, setting better than him
beginnings, the points at which things start

explanation.surface: A boast that the setter outdoes a rival setter, Serpent, at least in the opening clues.
explanation.walkthrough: Serpent is another setter of Independent crosswords; read as two words the answer says what one setter does to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Outsets are beginnings, the moments when things start, so they are starters.

clue.text: Possible description of sty could be stye?

definitions.meaning: a pigsty is an ugly, unsightly thing
a stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a sore on the eye

explanation.surface: A wordplay quibble on whether sty might be spelt stye.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one word the answer describes an ugly pigsty; split as EYE SORE it describes the eyelid infection.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an ugly sight, and a stye is literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Leninist leader released? Yahoo!

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: someone released from prison is out

explanation.surface: A cheer at the release of a Leninist leader from prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yahoo!' looks like a cry of joy, but it is the noun: Swift's brutish Yahoos in Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a coarse, boorish person, which is what a lout is.

clue.text: Postponed? Oh, Lovely!

parts.note: the exclamation oh is written as O
lovely means nice

explanation.surface: Someone hears that an event has been postponed and responds with heavy sarcasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan put on ice is held in reserve, suspended until later, so it has been postponed.

clue.text: Matter for revision by hospital department?

definitions.text: Matter for revision by hospital department?

indicators.note: revising something reworks it, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: Something a hospital department needs to review, presumably a patient's case.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer: what a hospital department revises is the care it gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the medical care that a hospital department reviews and revises for a patient.

clue.text: Absolutely astounded by peacenik in Derby?

indicators.note: the peace-lover is placed inside the hat

parts.note: a derby is the American name for a bowler hat
a dove is a person who favours peace rather than war

explanation.surface: Someone is astonished by a pacifist turning up in the city of Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby looks like the English city but is the American word for a bowler hat; 'in' puts the bird of peace inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bowled over is an idiom for being completely overwhelmed with surprise.

clue.text: A hospital department obstructing Doctor Hoskins going round

indicators.note: the doctor and setter get in the way of the department, blocking it by sitting inside it

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
the setter of this puzzle refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A hospital department is getting in the way of a doctor doing his rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Hoskins going round' looks like a ward round, but 'going round' is the definition; 'obstructing' puts doctor and setter inside the department.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes something present all around, such as ambient noise or temperature.

clue.text: Wearing retro Levis or elegant clothes

indicators.note: retro means backwards-looking, so the enclosed letters are read in reverse
used as a verb: the outer words clothe, or enclose, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Fashion advice: wear retro Levi's jeans, or else smart clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a verb, not the garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosive means wearing away gradually, as water wears stone.

clue.text: Those picked up in Hackney markets, I'm told

indicators.note: what one is told is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: fairs are markets, as in a trade fair

explanation.surface: Someone has heard about the markets in Hackney, a borough of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney looks like the London borough, but a hackney carriage is a licensed taxi, which picks up paying passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi's fares are the paying passengers it collects, those picked up by the cab.

clue.text: Booty fun? I'll put the kibosh on it!

definitions.text: I'll put the kibosh on it!

parts.note: booty is plunder, and spoil is an old word for it
sport means fun, as in 'just for sport'

explanation.surface: A killjoy declares an end to some fun, perhaps on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport is someone who ruins others' fun, the person who puts a stop to it.

clue.text: Soothing drug distributed to ill men

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug

indicators.note: something distributed is spread around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soothing medicine is handed out to sick men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges TO ILL MEN into MOLLIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient soothes and softens, whether a skin cream or a calming remark.

clue.text: Atrocious man popular round America

parts.note: a man is he
something popular is in
O is round in shape
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A terrible, much-loved man goes on tour around the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous means wicked and shocking, the same as atrocious.

clue.text: Rashly gave food to artist Damien for Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words have their starts exchanged

parts.note: to give food to is to feed, past tense fed
Damien Hirst is the British artist

explanation.surface: Someone recklessly fed Damien Hirst, the British artist famous for his pickled shark.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of FED HIRST gives HED FIRST, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting headfirst means plunging in without thought, which is acting rashly.

clue.text: Back, bottom or side but not centre

parts.note: the bottom of something is its end

indicators.note: the middle of the word is dropped, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for a massage or a body part: back, bottom or side, avoiding the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a body part, but it is the verb meaning to support.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a candidate or plan is to back it, giving it support.

clue.text: Drunk ordering a port in a foreign land

indicators.note: a drunk staggers around in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk orders a glass of port while abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink, but Rio Grande is a port city in southern Brazil; the A of 'a port' belongs to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio Grande is a seaport in Brazil, a harbour town in a foreign country.

clue.text: I glance about like one watching over you?

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone glancing around, like a person keeping an eye on you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges I GLANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel is said to watch over you, so being like one is angelic.

clue.text: Lips in blue, perhaps, or another colour

indicators.note: the edges are placed inside the abbreviation for the party

parts.note: blue is the colour of the UK Conservative party, abbreviated Con
the lips of cups or bowls are their rims

explanation.surface: Lips turned blue with cold, or perhaps some other colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' seems to be a colour but stands for Conservative; 'another colour' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep red, a different colour from the blue mentioned.

clue.text: Hoskins has to crack the king's disease or die

indicators.note: cracking something breaks into it, so the setter's possession goes inside the disease

parts.note: gout was traditionally the disease of kings, caused by rich living
the setter has is I've

explanation.surface: The setter must either break the curse of the king's disease or perish.
explanation.walkthrough: Gout is called the disease of kings, from rich food and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To give out is to stop working or fail, as an engine or a body dies.

clue.text: Understand I must expend energy to make love

parts.note: to understand something is to get it

indicators.note: spending energy uses it up, so the letter for energy goes

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone works out that lovemaking takes some effort.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the Roman numeral for one; ONE without E gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Get it on is slang for having sex, hence to make love.

clue.text: One following Long John Silver along the beach?

definitions.text: One following Long John Silver along the beach?

parts.words: One following Long John Silver along the beach
parts.note: the pirate of Treasure Island has a wooden leg, so on sand he leaves only one shoe print trailing behind him

explanation.walkthrough: 'One following' looks like a person tailing the pirate, but it is the single print his one good foot leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A footprint is the mark a foot leaves behind on sand, trailing after the walker.

clue.text: One likely to make Den more fiery in Walford?

indicators.note: Walford is the East End setting of the soap EastEnders, where Cockney speakers drop their h's

parts.note: something more fiery is hotter

explanation.surface: Someone stirring up the EastEnders character Den to make him angrier.
explanation.walkthrough: Den Watts was a famous EastEnders villain; here den is the lair an animal makes, and Cockney speech drops the H of HOTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Otters live in dens or holts by riverbanks, so one is likely to make a den.

clue.text: Country said to prefer game to duck

indicators.note: preferring one thing to another swaps it in, so the game replaces the duck

parts.note: something said aloud is oral rather than written
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Someone from the country says they like game birds better than duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' and 'duck' both seem to be meat, but game is rugby union, and duck is O, a zero cricket score.
explanation.definitionFit: Country used as an adjective, as in country life, means rural.

clue.text: Lean to drink last of fizz, being half-cut in Bow!

indicators.note: drinking takes a thing in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a ship that leans lists

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A slightly tipsy person in Bow leans over to sip their sparkling wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is in London's East End, home of Cockney rhyming slang, where Brahms and Liszt means pissed, or drunk; half of the phrase gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang Brahms and Liszt rhymes with pissed, so half the phrase stands for being drunk.

clue.text: Give back small profits

parts.note: to give something back is to return it
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Advice to give back modest earnings, perhaps to a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give back' looks like the definition, but it is wordplay; 'profits' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns are the gains yielded by an investment, so profits is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Fills undies with bit of radish as stuffing

indicators.note: stuffing is put inside something, so the letter goes in

parts.note: thongs are skimpy underwear

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs underwear with radish, for reasons best left unexplored.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowds that throng a place fill it, packing it with people.

clue.text: Short break in Rome is the thing

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: a break is a rest

explanation.surface: A short break in Rome is the thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is the thing' sounds like approval of a city break, but res is the Latin word for thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Res is Latin for thing, as in res publica, so in Rome it is the thing.

clue.text: Republican's opening play with May?

indicators.note: the abbreviation opens up the word for play, sitting inside it

parts.note: to play with something is to toy with it

explanation.surface: A Republican's first move is to flirt with somebody named May.
explanation.walkthrough: May is Theresa May, the former UK Conservative prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party, the party Theresa May led.

clue.text: Where loafers should really be standing

definitions.text: Where loafers should really be standing

parts.words: Where loafers should really be standing
parts.note: loafers are slip-on shoes worn standing up, and idlers who should be up and working

explanation.walkthrough: Loafers are both idle people, who should be up working, and slip-on shoes, which belong where you stand.
explanation.definitionFit: To be standing upright, active and busy, is the idiom used of loafers here.
